name: GBE1 (GBED)
summary: GBE1, on chromosome 26 (26q12-q13): glycogen branching enzyme deficiency (GBED), a fatal recessive metabolic disease of the Quarter Horse and related breeds. The enzyme makes the branch points in glycogen, the body's store of glucose. One base change in exon 1 (c.102C>A, p.Tyr34Ter) puts a stop early in the protein, so no working enzyme is made. A foal with two copies is aborted late, stillborn, or dies soon after birth. A carrier has about half the normal enzyme activity and is otherwise normal, with no established effect on coat, build or performance, so the allele persists only through carriers. It traces to a single founder and is found mainly in American Quarter Horses, American Paint Horses and horses with Quarter Horse ancestry. UC Davis reports the genotypes as N/N, N/G and G/G; this is the only recognised disease allele of GBE1 in horses.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: GBE1 (GBED) carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy of the GBED allele. The horse has roughly half the normal enzyme activity and is otherwise healthy, with nothing to see. Half its foals inherit the copy, and a foal is affected only when both parents pass it on.

phenotypes.name: Glycogen branching enzyme deficiency
phenotypes.description: Tissues cannot build normally branched glycogen, so they cannot store and release energy properly; skeletal muscle, heart muscle, liver and brain suffer most. Reported outcomes are late-term abortion, stillbirth, or a weak foal with muscle weakness and seizures that dies soon after birth. No affected horse reaches adulthood.

frequencies.population: American Quarter Horse (about 8.3% carriers, UC Davis's estimate; a 2006 study's allele frequency of about 4.1% among registered horses agrees with it)
American Paint Horse (about 7.1% carriers, UC Davis's estimate; a 2006 study's allele frequency of about 3.6% agrees with it)
Thoroughbred (allele not found in a 2006 study)
